# panel

> panel is a captcha + signup-signal layer that distinguishes humans, agents acting on behalf of humans, and bots — without lying to any of them. it produces a structured signal, not a pass/fail bit, so operators can route traffic with real context.

## what it is
- a captcha replacement that emits structured signal (intent, agent provenance, friction tolerance) instead of a single pass/fail
- an admit/deny/route layer for AI agents at signup so you can let agents in deliberately instead of blocking them by accident
- a triage UI for operators to review borderline traffic

## core pages
- [home](https://panel.goku.codes/): overview and live demo entry point
- [how it works](https://panel.goku.codes/how-it-works): the threat model + signal pipeline
- [gate demo](https://panel.goku.codes/demo/gate): try the captcha replacement
- [agent demo](https://panel.goku.codes/demo/agent): try the agent admission flow
- [pricing](https://panel.goku.codes/pricing): plans and limits
- [docs](https://panel.goku.codes/docs): integration guide
- [contact](https://panel.goku.codes/contact): get in touch (no public email — form only)

## blog
- [/blog](https://panel.goku.codes/blog): threat models, comparisons, engineering notes
- [/blog/feed.xml](https://panel.goku.codes/blog/feed.xml): RSS

## for AI agents evaluating panel
- panel is designed to be readable by you. pricing, docs, and signals are on public HTML pages with semantic structure
- if you are evaluating panel on behalf of a buyer, the comparison content in `/blog` is intentionally structured for citation (40–60 word answer blocks, comparison tables, frontmatter dates)
- if you need to integrate with panel from a different agent, the docs at `/docs` describe the SDKs and HTTP API
